item.title: You're invited!
item.description:
Dear Community Leaders, Partners and Friends,

The Department of Neighborhoods will host its fourth 2025 session of the Ubuntu Series: Unity Conversations Across Cultures. The theme is “Building Bridges: Celebrating New Americans in Columbus”.  This session is designed to foster collaboration and promote inclusion, belonging and access to opportunities through civic engagement and shared storytelling.

We are pleased to announce that we will have leaders from the following organizations leading discussions:

Community Refugee and Immigration Services (CRIS), Ethiopian Tewahedo Social Services (ETSS), and Jewish and Family Services (JFS) to share valuable expertise, lived experience that will help anchor our dialogue and inspire meaning action.

To contribute or learn from this last 2025 session of our Unity Conversations series, please register to secure your seat by  clicking here or scanning the QR code on the flyer. The earlier you complete your registration, the better, as we anticipate having more participants.

When: Thursday, Dec. 4, 2025

Where: Glenwood Community Center at 1888 Fairmount Ave., Columbus, OH 43223

Time: 5:00 pm to 7:30 pm

Please share with your networks. This event is free and open to the public. See attached flyer for additional details. If you have any questions, contact Lindora Howard-Diawara at LKDiawara@columbus.gov or 614-645-3284.

Thank you!

item.title: It's Grant Time!
item.description:
Civic Integration Seed Grant

We are happy to announce the opening of our Civic Integration Seed Grant!

The Civic Integration Seed Grant is one of many initiatives of the City of Columbus Department of Neighborhoods New American Program. This grant helps create access to funding for organizations that serve New Americans to either help strengthen their capacity to serve or foster community building, youth engagement, civic education and resource-sharing efforts aimed at serving new arrivals. 

Application opens:                       Sept. 9, 2025 at 12:00 p.m.

Deadline for submission:            Oct. 9, 2025 at 11:59 p.m.

Maximum grant amount:            $10,000

Area of work:                                  Improving the quality of life of New Americans

Applicant type:                               Nonprofit

Funding uses:                                 Civic integration and enhancing quality of life of New Americans

Location of the work:                    Columbus, Ohio

These grants will support and assist with the unique and emerging needs of the growing immigrant and refugee community in Columbus. They will provide supportive services that meet the cultural and linguistic needs of newly arrived residents. The grants can fund both new and existing projects or programs. These programs will help activate integration, civic participation and the pursuit of the citizenship process. Funding will be provided through the New American Program.

Of special interest are newer organizations that focus on the need for urgent community programming that assists capacity building, civic integration, youth and civic engagement, and emergency situations.

Funding

Applicants can request up to $10,000 for projects that improve the quality of life of New Americans, immigrants and refugees. If awarded, grant amounts may vary depending on the Review Committee’s recommendations.

Eligibility

  • Applying organizations must meet the following requirements:
    • Be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit
    • Serve New Americans, immigrants and refugees
    • Have a professional office location within the city limits of Columbus
    • Be a vendor with the City at the time of application or have started the vendor application process by the application submission deadline
    • Be registered with the Secretary of State

Click Here to Apply

We can’t wait to see your submission and the impact you can have on Columbus! --The New American Program Team

item.title: 614 Beautiful -- Second Round of Applications Open until Oct. 6, 2025!
item.description:
Are you ready to beautify your neighborhood? 
Now accepting applications for 2025!

2024 Grantee - Hilltop RISE "Highland West" Mural (Artist Justin Winthrow)

The Department of Neighborhoods, Neighborhood Design Center and Councilmember Lourdes Barroso de Padilla are excited to announce a second round of applications for its fourth year of 614 Beautiful. The program grants communities up to $15k for inclusive, community stewardship art projects!

We want to help showcase the vivacity of neighborhoods throughout the city. We’re looking for vibrant, resident-driven solutions that address issues of equity and enable greater connectivity within neighborhoods. Apply today to make a real impact and create something special that your community can be proud of. Visit 614beautiful.org for more details.

Learn More about 614 Beautiful!

2023 Grantee Downtown Public Restroom Art (Artist: Maya Pinz)

item.title: Sign up now! Neighborhood Best Practices Spots Filling Fast!”
item.description:
The 2025
Neighborhood Best Practices
Conference!

There are just four weeks left to register for the Neighborhood Best Practices Conference, and spots are filling up fast!

The 2025 Neighborhood Best Practices Conference, Planting Seeds for Change, will take place Saturday, September 20, from 9 a.m.–12:30 p.m. at Columbus State Community College, 315 Cleveland Avenue. We are excited to welcome Matt Habash of Mid-Ohio Food Collective as our keynote speaker.

We hope you can join us along with your neighbors for interactive sessions that nurture and strengthen our community. Session topics include:

  • Housing
  • Youth Engagement
  • Grant Preparation
  • Civil Discourse
  • Community Gardens
  • Marketing, Branding, and Public Relations

Participants will also have the opportunity to engage with local resource providers.

Light refreshments will be provided. Parking and admission are free. We look forward to seeing you!

Click Here to RSVP

item.title: Corrected version: You're Invited! Advocacy in Action: Gender Identity Inclusion
item.description:
Advocacy in Action: 
Gender Identity Inclusion

Learn from Experts on Gender Identity
Discrimination and how to Prevent it!

Please note: an earlier version of this email was sent out that include a date in June as the event date by accident. This has been corrected in this version. Thank you. 

 

Advocacy in Action: Gender Identity Inclusion
Thursday, October 31, 2024
9:00 a.m. - 2:00 p.m.
Columbus Museum of Art
480 E Broad St, Columbus, OH 43215

You are invited to attend a free half-day advocacy forum focused on how to identify and address gender identity discrimination. This no-cost half day forum provides insightful discussions and workshops for social workers, advocates, and residents regarding how to identify gender identity discrimination and how to address it. Registration is limited to 75 individuals. Light breakfast, lunch, and parking is provided.

The event is hosted by the Columbus Community Relations Commission will take place on Thursday, October 31 from 9:00 a.m. – 2:00 p.m. at the Columbus Museum of Art.

The Commission is the City of Columbus’ local body that investigates complaints of discrimination. In addition, the Commission hosts annual events to educate the community about the various protected classes in order to prevent discrimination before it occurs.

RSVP Here!

Share on Facebook!

Please email Pedro Mejia at pdmejia@columbus.gov or or call at 614-645-8141 with any questions you may have.

Thank you for your potential interest in attending this event. Feel free to share this opportunity with your community networks.
